overview_description:
Introduction
We operate a central distribution network with seven independent, disjoint sites. A central coordinator oversees system-wide policies, resource pools, and performance targets while each site runs its operations autonomously.

Problem Structure
The planning model is organized as a block-separated set of site-level decision problems. Each site makes local decisions under its own operating rules and conditions, independent of other sites. The overall formulation reflects a block-diagonal structure, enabling parallel analysis and execution at the site level without direct cross-site decision coupling.

Coordination
A hierarchical coordination framework guides the system. The central coordinator issues policy signals and resource allocations, collects summarized performance feedback from each site, and rebalances directives to align local actions with enterprise priorities. Communication is streamlined: sites optimize locally in response to guidance, and the coordinator aggregates outcomes, resolves trade-offs, and enforces consistency across sites. This approach preserves autonomy, supports scalable parallel optimization, and maintains governance, fairness, and strategic alignment.

Objective
The enterprise-level objective is to maximize overall system performance. The central coordinator steers local decisions toward this goal by adjusting allocations and policies, ensuring that site-level feasibility and organizational guidelines are respected while driving the system to its best achievable outcome.
